feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Mayor of Bend shares how her community is doing after elementary school shooting
entry.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Mayor of Bend Melanie Kebler about how the community is grieving the three children and teacher who were killed in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School on Thursday.

entry.title: Here's what experts say about the civilian intervention in the Bend school shooting
entry.summary: An armed bystander stopped a shooting at a school in Bend, Ore. We talk with experts about how rarely an armed civilian ends an attack like this and how gun rights groups are responding.

entry.title: 'Where is Austin Tice': NPR series investigates a journalist's disappearance in Syria
entry.summary: A new investigative series by NPR looks into the real life missing person case of American journalist Austin Tice, who disappeared in Syria over a decade ago.

entry.title: On 'Dopamine Chamber,' Irish band Fontaines D.C. finds beauty in chaos
entry.summary: The Irish rock band Fontaines D.C. has been trying to make sense of it in their music. Their new album is called Dopamine Chamber.

entry.title: At SF Tech Week, a vibe check on how people in Silicon Valley feel about the AI boom
entry.summary: In Silicon Valley, the AI boom means a lot of people are excited about this new technology, but concerned about when the music might stop. NPR went to San Francisco Tech Week to take the pulse.

entry.title: Norway faces public dilemma over divesting from companies involved with war in Gaza
entry.summary: Norway has the world's largest sovereign wealth fund, but it's facing a self-imposed dilemma. Should the fund's investments include companies that contribute to the ongoing Israel-Hamas war?

entry.title: A Kelvin wave is raising sea levels along the West Coast
entry.summary: A massive deep-ocean wave is raising sea levels along the West Coast. It's called a Kelvin Wave, and it's driven by El Nino

entry.title: Midterm ad spending climbed over $10 billion this week, what does it buy?
entry.summary: Money is pouring into political races across the country, but are there limits to how much the extra cash can do to sway the outcome of the midterms.

entry.title: Health insurers balk at paying for newborns' RSV immunization in the hospital
entry.summary: Many infants are leaving the hospital without getting immunized against RSV. Why? Because many insurance companies won't pay for the shots while the newborn is in the hospital.

entry.title: 'Washington Post' photographer recounts Israeli settler attack
entry.summary: Washington Post freelance photographer Heidi Levine was attacked by Israeli settlers in the West Bank. Levine speaks with NPR's Scott Detrow about the attack.
